holidays.name: National Pizza with the Works Except Anchovies Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate a loaded pizza piled with every topping you love, minus the salty little fish that divide dinner tables. Order a pie with pepperoni, sausage, peppers, mushrooms, and onions, and leave the anchovies off.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin, and it has become a yearly fixture on pizza lovers' calendars.
holidays.funFact: Anchovies are among the most polarizing pizza toppings, and plenty of pizzerias list them as an optional add-on so the rest of the pie can stay crowd-pleasing.

holidays.name: American Fancy Rat & Mouse Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate pet rats and mice, which are clever, social, and affectionate companions. Fans celebrate with treats, cage makeovers, and a lot of whisker-twitching admiration.
holidays.origin: The observance is tied to the American Fancy Rat and Mouse Association, which promotes responsible ownership and the hobby of keeping fancy rats and mice as pets.
holidays.funFact: Pet rats can learn their names and tricks, and they are known to make a chattering sound called bruxing when they are happy.

holidays.name: National French Dip Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the beloved sandwich of thinly sliced roast beef on a crusty roll, served with a cup of savory au jus for dunking. Each bite is a delicious, dripping delight.
holidays.origin: The sandwich is traditionally credited to Los Angeles, where two rival restaurants, Philippe the Original and Cole's, both claim to have invented it in the early 20th century. The day itself is an unofficial observance of unclear origin.
holidays.funFact: Both Philippe the Original and Cole's still serve French dips in Los Angeles, so you can sample each and decide which claim to the title you believe.
